words.enDefinition: the first romantic meeting between two people

examples.en: Our first date was at the little café opposite the campus bookshop last spring.
examples.zh: 去年春天，我们的「第一次约会」是在校园书店对面的小咖啡馆。

examples.en: She suggested a walk for their first date because both of them liked being outdoors.
examples.zh: 她建议两人的「第一次约会」去散步，因为他们都喜欢户外。

words.zhGloss: 见面前互不相识的约会
words.enDefinition: a romantic meeting arranged for two people who have never met each other
acceptedZhAnswers: 见面前互不相识的约会

examples.en: My flatmate set up a blind date for me with someone from her course.
examples.zh: 室友安排我和她课上的一名同学来一次「见面前互不相识的约会」。

examples.en: He was nervous about the blind date until they started talking about their classes.
examples.zh: 开始聊各自的课之前，他一直对这次「见面前互不相识的约会」有些紧张。

collocations: meet someone on a blind date

words.enDefinition: a date on which two couples go somewhere together

examples.en: We planned a double date with my roommate and her boyfriend after exams.
examples.zh: 考试后，我们安排了和我室友及她男朋友「两对人一起约会」。

examples.en: Our double date ended with four of us sharing chips outside the cinema.
examples.zh: 「两对人一起约会」的最后，我们四人在电影院外分吃了一份薯条。

collocations: invite someone on a double date

words.enDefinition: an informal romantic meeting over coffee or a similar drink

examples.en: I suggested a coffee date because we only had an hour between our classes.
examples.zh: 我们两节课之间只有一个小时，我就提议来一次「喝咖啡的约会」。

examples.en: Their coffee date turned into an afternoon walk around the university's botanical garden.
examples.zh: 他们的「喝咖啡的约会」后来变成了下午在大学植物园散步。

words.enDefinition: an evening a couple sets aside to spend time together

examples.en: We moved date night to Thursday because my partner had an essay due Friday.
examples.zh: 伴侣周五要交论文，所以我们把「两人专门约会的晚上」改到了周四。

examples.en: Our date night was just homemade pizza and a movie in the living room.
examples.zh: 我们的「两人约会之夜」只是在客厅吃自制披萨、看电影。

words.enDefinition: to meet someone socially with a possible romantic interest

examples.en: I hadn't planned to go on a date during the first week of term.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算在开学第一周「去约会」。

examples.en: Leo asked whether I wanted to go on a date after our seminar ended.
examples.zh: 利奥问我，研讨课结束后想不想「去约会」。

collocations: ask someone to go on a date
go on a date with someone

words.enDefinition: to have an ongoing romantic relationship with someone

examples.en: I didn't expect to go out with someone from my own course this year.
examples.zh: 我没想到今年会「和同一门课的人交往」。

examples.en: She said she didn't want to go out with someone who lived far away.
examples.zh: 她说不想「和住得很远的人交往」。

collocations: decide to go out with someone
go out with someone for months
go out with someone from class

words.enDefinition: an informal question asking if someone is currently dating another person

examples.en: My friend asked, “Are you seeing anyone at the moment, or are you single?”
examples.zh: 朋友问：“「你现在在和人交往吗」，还是单身？”

examples.en: “Are you seeing anyone these days?” she asked while we waited for our drinks.
examples.zh: 等饮料时她问：“「你最近在和人交往吗」？”

collocations: are you seeing anyone at the moment
are you seeing anyone these days
ask if someone is seeing anyone

words.expression: would you like to go out
words.lemma: would you like to go out
words.enDefinition: a polite invitation to spend time together as a possible romantic date
acceptedEnVariants: would you like to go out

examples.en: “Would you like to go out with me after our last lecture on Friday?”
examples.zh: “周五最后一节课后，「你愿意跟我约会吗」？”

examples.en: After we finished our coffee, she asked, “Would you like to go out sometime?”
examples.zh: 喝完咖啡后她问：“「你愿意找个时间跟我约会吗」？”

collocations: would you like to go out sometime
would you like to go out with me
would you like to go out for dinner

words.enDefinition: to say no to an invitation to go on a date

examples.en: She decided to turn down a date because she wasn't interested in meeting that way.
examples.zh: 她对这种见面方式没有兴趣，决定「谢绝约会邀请」。

examples.en: I felt awkward when I had to turn down a date with someone from class.
examples.zh: 我不得不「谢绝同班同学的约会邀请」时，觉得有些尴尬。

collocations: turn down a date with someone
decide to turn down a date

words.enDefinition: to invite and accompany another person on a romantic outing

examples.en: I had never wanted to take someone on a date until we met at the films.
examples.zh: 直到在电影放映时遇见对方，我才第一次想「带个人去约会」。

examples.en: Where would you take someone on a date if you both liked quiet places?
examples.zh: 如果两个人都喜欢安静的地方，你会「带对方去哪里约会」？

collocations: take someone on a date downtown
offer to take someone on a date
take someone on a date to the cinema

words.enDefinition: to rearrange a planned romantic meeting for a different time

examples.en: We had to reschedule a date when my lab session ran over that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午实验课超时，我们不得不「改约会时间」。

examples.en: I asked whether we could reschedule a date for the following week after exams.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「改约会时间」，放到考完试的下一周。

words.enDefinition: a place people like to go for a romantic meeting

examples.en: We found a quiet date spot near campus that stayed open after lectures.
examples.zh: 我们在校园附近找到一个安静的「适合约会的地点」，下课后还营业。

examples.en: My friend suggested a date spot within walking distance of our residence.
examples.zh: 朋友推荐了一个「适合约会的地点」，从宿舍走路就能到。

words.enDefinition: anxiety or uneasiness before or during a first romantic date

examples.en: My first-date nerves faded once we started talking about films near the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆旁聊起电影后，我「第一次约会时的紧张」渐渐消失了。

examples.en: She went for a walk beforehand to settle her first-date nerves that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，她事先散了会儿步，缓解「第一次约会时的紧张」。

words.enDefinition: to pay for another person's dinner as a kind gesture

examples.en: I'd like to treat you to dinner after we finish our last group project.
examples.zh: 最后一个小组项目做完后，我想「请你吃晚饭」。

examples.en: Can I treat you to dinner at the noodle place after your evening lab?
examples.zh: 你晚上的实验课结束后，我能在那家面馆「请你吃晚饭」吗？

collocations: offer to treat someone to dinner
treat you to dinner this weekend

words.expression: I'd like to see you again
words.lemma: i'd like to see you again
words.enDefinition: a direct way to say you would enjoy another meeting or date
acceptedEnVariants: I'd like to see you again
I would like to see you again

examples.en: “I'd like to see you again,” he said as we walked to the bus stop.
examples.zh: 走去公交站时他说：“「我想再和你见面」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “I'd like to see you again if you're also free next week.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“如果你下周也有空，「我想再和你见面」。”

collocations: I'd like to see you again sometime
I'd like to see you again next week
I'd like to see you again if you're interested

words.enDefinition: a friendly way to say you enjoyed an outing with someone

examples.en: I texted, “I had a lovely time at the exhibition, thanks for asking me.”
examples.zh: 我发消息说：“看展时「我玩得很开心」，谢谢你约我。”

examples.en: “I had a lovely time tonight,” she said before heading back to her residence.
examples.zh: 回宿舍前她说：“今晚「我玩得很开心」。”

collocations: I had a lovely time tonight
I had a lovely time with you
I had a lovely time at dinner

words.enDefinition: to continue without deciding in advance how a relationship will develop

examples.en: We agreed to see where things go after getting coffee a couple of times.
examples.zh: 喝了几次咖啡后，我们同意先「看看关系会怎么发展」。

examples.en: I wanted to see where things go before calling it a serious relationship.
examples.zh: 我想先「看看关系会怎么发展」，再把它称为认真的恋爱关系。

collocations: take it easy and see where things go
agree to see where things go
want to see where things go

words.enDefinition: to let a romantic relationship develop without rushing decisions or commitments

examples.en: I said I wanted to take things slowly because we had only just met.
examples.zh: 我说想「慢慢发展关系」，因为我们刚认识。

examples.en: They agreed to take things slowly while settling into life on a new campus.
examples.zh: 他们同意在适应新校园生活的同时「慢慢发展关系」。

words.enDefinition: to feel a natural romantic attraction or connection with each other

examples.en: They have chemistry, judging by the way they laugh at the same jokes.
examples.zh: 看他们被同样的玩笑逗笑的样子，两人确实「彼此来电」。

examples.en: You can have chemistry with someone even if your lives are quite different.
examples.zh: 即使生活方式很不同，两个人也可能「彼此来电」。

collocations: have chemistry on a first date

words.enDefinition: a feeling of romantic interest that two people share towards each other

examples.en: Their mutual attraction surprised both of them after years on the same course.
examples.zh: 同上一门课多年后，两人发现彼此「相互吸引」，都感到意外。

examples.en: They talked about the mutual attraction only when a friend brought it up.
examples.zh: 朋友提起后，他们才聊到彼此「相互吸引」的事。

words.enDefinition: to feel strongly attracted to someone, often without telling them

examples.en: I used to have a crush on someone who sat beside me in lectures.
examples.zh: 我以前「对一个上大课时坐在我旁边的人心动过」。

examples.en: You can have a crush on a friend and still want to take things slowly.
examples.zh: 你可能「对一个朋友心动」，同时仍想慢慢发展关系。

collocations: have a crush on a classmate
admit you have a crush on someone

words.enDefinition: to begin to feel strong romantic affection for someone

examples.en: I never expected to fall for someone during my first summer away from home.
examples.zh: 我没想到第一次离家过暑假时会「爱上某人」。

examples.en: It's possible to fall for someone after knowing them as a friend for years.
examples.zh: 认识多年的朋友也有可能让你「爱上对方」。

words.enDefinition: to be romantically interested in a person, in informal speech

examples.en: I didn't expect to be into someone from my study group at all.
examples.zh: 我完全没想到会「喜欢上学习小组里的人」。

examples.en: You can be into someone and still decide a relationship isn't right for you.
examples.zh: 你可能「喜欢某个人」，同时觉得建立恋爱关系不适合自己。

words.enDefinition: to feel romantically attracted to someone, especially in informal British English

examples.en: I didn't expect to fancy someone from my course after spending so much time together.
examples.zh: 相处这么长时间后，我没想到会「对同一门课的人有好感」。

examples.en: My flatmate joked that you can fancy someone before learning their name or course.
examples.zh: 室友开玩笑说，还不知道名字或专业，也可能「对一个人有好感」。

words.enDefinition: informal dating slang for starting to feel romantic affection, often unexpectedly

examples.en: I didn't think I'd catch feelings after meeting him for coffee on campus twice.
examples.zh: 在学校和他喝了两次咖啡，我没想到自己会「开始动心」。

examples.en: She told her roommate she might catch feelings if they kept spending weekends together.
examples.zh: 她跟室友说，如果两人继续一起过周末，她可能会「开始动心」。

words.enDefinition: interest in someone as a possible romantic partner

examples.en: I wasn't sure whether the invitation showed romantic interest or just friendly curiosity.
examples.zh: 我不确定那次邀请是出于「恋爱方面的好感」，还是朋友间的好奇。

examples.en: He made his romantic interest clear when he asked her on a proper date.
examples.zh: 他正式约她出去时，把自己的「恋爱方面的好感」表达清楚了。

words.enDefinition: to feel romantic affection towards a particular person

examples.en: I knew I might have feelings for him when I missed our Sunday walks.
examples.zh: 我开始想念周日一起散步时，就意识到自己可能「对他有爱慕之情」。

examples.en: She asked what to do if you have feelings for a close friend from class.
examples.zh: 她问，如果「对一位关系很好的同学有爱慕之情」，该怎么办。

collocations: admit you have feelings for someone

words.enDefinition: to act playfully in a way that suggests romantic interest

examples.en: He used to flirt with her by making silly jokes during our coffee breaks.
examples.zh: 我们课间喝咖啡时，他以前总爱逗她，跟她「调情」。

examples.en: I couldn't tell whether she meant to flirt or was just being friendly.
examples.zh: 我分不清她是有意「调情」，还是单纯友好。

words.enDefinition: playfully showing that you may be romantically interested in someone

examples.en: His message sounded flirty to me, but my roommate read it differently.
examples.zh: 我觉得他的消息「带有调情意味」，室友却有不同的理解。

examples.en: They exchanged flirty jokes while waiting for the outdoor film to start that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚等露天电影开场时，他们互相开了些「带有调情意味」的玩笑。

words.enDefinition: something important enough to make someone decide against a relationship or agreement

examples.en: Being unable to agree on where to live might be a deal-breaker for them.
examples.zh: 无法就住在哪里达成一致，对他们来说可能是「无法接受的条件」。

examples.en: She thought very different plans after graduation could become a deal-breaker in their relationship.
examples.zh: 她觉得毕业后的计划差别太大，可能会成为恋爱里「让人无法接受的条件」。

words.enDefinition: an informal term for a sign that someone may be a considerate partner

examples.en: For me, listening carefully when someone disagrees is a green flag in a relationship.
examples.zh: 对我而言，遇到不同意见时能认真倾听，是恋爱中「值得肯定的信号」。

examples.en: She saw it as a green flag when her date respected the change of plans.
examples.zh: 约会对象尊重了她更改计划的决定，她认为这是个「值得肯定的信号」。

collocations: see something as a green flag

words.enDefinition: to behave in ways that suggest conflicting levels of interest or intention

examples.en: I didn't want to send mixed signals by accepting another date out of politeness.
examples.zh: 我不想出于礼貌接受下次约会，给对方「发出矛盾信号」。

examples.en: She thought he might send mixed signals without realising how she read his messages.
examples.zh: 她觉得，他可能无意中「发出矛盾信号」，不知道她会怎样理解这些消息。

collocations: send mixed signals about a relationship
try not to send mixed signals

words.enDefinition: to interpret clues in someone's actions to understand their intentions or feelings

examples.en: I tried to read the signs but still couldn't tell how he felt.
examples.zh: 我试着「从迹象作出判断」，还是看不出他怎么想。

examples.en: Rather than read the signs from brief messages, she asked whether he was interested.
examples.zh: 她直接问他有没有兴趣，没再「从几条简短消息里的迹象作判断」。

words.enDefinition: to encourage someone to believe you are romantically interested when you are not

examples.en: I didn't want to lead someone on by agreeing to go out again.
examples.zh: 我不想答应再约，「让对方误以为我有意」。

examples.en: You can lead someone on if your actions suggest promises you do not mean.
examples.zh: 如果你的行为暗示了自己无意兑现的承诺，就可能「让对方误以为你对其有意」。

collocations: try not to lead someone on

words.enDefinition: romantic love that the other person does not return

examples.en: The campus play told a funny story about unrequited love between two old friends.
examples.zh: 校园戏剧讲了两个老朋友之间「得不到回应的爱」，故事很有趣。

examples.en: He used to write songs about unrequited love when he first moved here.
examples.zh: 他刚搬来的时候，经常写关于「得不到回应的爱」的歌。

words.expression: I'm not looking for a relationship
words.lemma: i'm not looking for a relationship
words.enDefinition: a direct way to say you are not seeking a romantic commitment
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not looking for a relationship
I am not looking for a relationship

examples.en: “I'm not looking for a relationship right now,” she said after they finished coffee.
examples.zh: 喝完咖啡后，她说：“「我现在不想谈恋爱」。”

examples.en: I said, “I'm not looking for a relationship while I'm finishing my degree.”
examples.zh: 我说：“完成学位之前，「我现在不想谈恋爱」。”

collocations: I'm not looking for a relationship right now
I'm not looking for a relationship at the moment
I'm not looking for a relationship this year

words.enDefinition: not feeling prepared to start going on romantic dates

examples.en: He said he was not ready to date after ending a long relationship.
examples.zh: 结束一段长期恋情后，他说自己「还没准备好约会」。

examples.en: I told my friend I was not ready to date anyone from our class.
examples.zh: 我告诉朋友，自己「还没准备好和班里的人约会」。

collocations: feel like you're not ready to date
still not ready to date again

words.enDefinition: going on dates without agreeing to a committed relationship

examples.en: They both preferred casual dating while getting used to their new university schedules.
examples.zh: 在适应大学的新课表时，两人都更倾向于「非正式交往」。

examples.en: She explained what casual dating meant to her before they made any plans together.
examples.zh: 两人一起做任何安排前，她说清楚了「非正式交往」对她意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: meeting potential romantic partners through the internet

examples.en: My roommate tried online dating after moving somewhere she didn't know many people.
examples.zh: 室友搬到没多少熟人的地方后，尝试了「网上交友约会」。

examples.en: We talked about how online dating felt different from meeting someone through our friends.
examples.zh: 我们聊到「网上交友约会」和经朋友介绍认识人的感受有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: an app people use to meet potential romantic partners

examples.en: We first spoke on a dating app while studying at different universities nearby.
examples.zh: 我们在附近不同大学读书时，最先是在「约会交友应用」上开始聊天的。

examples.en: Maya deleted the dating app after deciding she wanted a break from meeting people.
examples.zh: 玛雅决定暂停认识新人后，删除了「约会交友应用」。

words.enDefinition: the page describing a person to others on a dating service

examples.en: My dating profile says I like quiet cafés and walks near the river.
examples.zh: 我的「约会交友资料」写着，我喜欢安静的咖啡馆和河边散步。

examples.en: I updated my dating profile after I moved to a new part of town.
examples.zh: 搬到城里新的片区后，我更新了「约会交友资料」。

words.enDefinition: a question or opening line offered to help someone fill in a profile

examples.en: I chose a profile prompt that let me write about my favourite campus café.
examples.zh: 我选了一道「个人资料回答题」，可以写我最喜欢的校园咖啡馆。

examples.en: Her answer to the profile prompt gave me something specific to ask about.
examples.zh: 她对那道「个人资料回答题」的回答，让我有了一个具体的话题可以问。

words.enDefinition: a match recorded after two dating app users express interest in each other

examples.en: The app showed a mutual match after they each liked the other's profile.
examples.zh: 两人各自点了对方资料的喜欢后，应用显示「双方互选配对」。

examples.en: I noticed the mutual match notification when I checked my phone between classes.
examples.zh: 两节课之间查手机时，我看到了「双方互选配对」的通知。

words.enDefinition: to be connected to another person by a dating app after showing interest

examples.en: I didn't expect to match with someone who went to the same university.
examples.zh: 我没想到会「与同一所大学的人配对成功」。

examples.en: Can you match with someone without seeing their whole profile in this app?
examples.zh: 在这个应用里，不看完整资料也能「与某人配对成功」吗？

collocations: match with someone on a dating app

words.enDefinition: to initiate a conversation by sending the first written message

examples.en: I wasn't sure whether to send the first message after we matched yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天配对后，我一时拿不准要不要「先发消息搭话」。

examples.en: She suggested I send the first message about something we'd both put in our profiles.
examples.zh: 她建议我「先发消息搭话」，说说我们资料里都提到的一个事。

collocations: decide to send the first message
feel ready to send the first message
ask who should send the first message

words.enDefinition: on some dating apps, to move a profile left to pass over it

examples.en: I didn't mean to swipe left before reading the rest of the profile.
examples.zh: 我本想看完剩下的资料，不是故意「向左划表示不感兴趣」。

examples.en: The app instructions showed how to swipe left when you want to skip a profile.
examples.zh: 应用说明演示了想跳过一份资料时怎样「向左划表示不感兴趣」。

words.enDefinition: on some dating apps, to move a profile right to show interest

examples.en: My flatmate told me what swipe right meant when I first tried the app.
examples.zh: 我第一次用这个应用时，室友告诉了我「向右划表示感兴趣」的意思。

examples.en: I decided to swipe right after seeing that we both loved old films.
examples.zh: 看见我们都爱老电影后，我决定「向右划表示感兴趣」。

words.enDefinition: the qualities or circumstances someone looks for in people they might date

examples.en: I adjusted my dating preferences after moving closer to the main university campus.
examples.zh: 搬到离主校区更近的地方后，我调整了「约会偏好」。

examples.en: They talked about dating preferences with friends on their way home from the film.
examples.zh: 看完电影回家的路上，他们和朋友聊了「约会偏好」。

words.enDefinition: what someone hopes to find or develop in a romantic relationship

examples.en: We talked about relationship goals after realising we wanted different things for next year.
examples.zh: 意识到对明年的期望不同后，我们聊了「期望的恋爱方向」。

examples.en: The profile asked about relationship goals alongside hobbies and places people liked to visit.
examples.zh: 个人资料除了问爱好和喜欢去的地方，还问「期望的恋爱方向」。

words.enDefinition: to arrange for a person to meet someone who might become their partner

examples.en: My sister loves to set someone up whenever two people in her club get along.
examples.zh: 姐姐社团里只要有两个人合得来，她就喜欢「给人介绍约会对象」。

examples.en: Would you set someone up if you knew both people wanted to meet?
examples.zh: 如果知道两人都想认识对方，你会「给人介绍约会对象」吗？

collocations: set a friend up with someone

words.enDefinition: to try to bring two people together as potential romantic partners

examples.en: Our friends liked to play matchmaker whenever we mentioned someone from the film club.
examples.zh: 我们提到电影社里的人，朋友就爱「当红娘牵线」。

examples.en: I promised not to play matchmaker unless both of them asked for an introduction.
examples.zh: 我答应除非两人都要求介绍，否则不「当红娘牵线」。

words.enDefinition: an event where people have several short meetings with possible partners

examples.en: The student union advertised speed dating as part of an evening of social events.
examples.zh: 学生会宣传晚间社交活动时，把「快速轮换式约会」列为其中一项。

examples.en: I tried speed dating once and met someone from a course I'd considered taking.
examples.zh: 我试过一次「快速轮换式约会」，遇到了一位读我考虑过的课程的人。

words.enDefinition: a social event intended for people who are not currently in a relationship

examples.en: We heard about the singles event when we passed the café near campus.
examples.zh: 经过校园附近那家咖啡馆时，我们听说了那场「单身交友活动」。

examples.en: My friend agreed to come to the singles event so I wouldn't arrive alone.
examples.zh: 朋友答应一起去「单身交友活动」，这样我就不用一个人到场。

words.enDefinition: to arrange an in-person meeting somewhere open to other people

examples.en: They agreed to meet in a public place near the main campus entrance.
examples.zh: 他们约好「在公共场所见面」，就在主校区入口附近。

examples.en: I suggested we meet in a public place both of us already knew.
examples.zh: 我建议「在两人都熟悉的公共场所见面」。

collocations: agree to meet in a public place
choose to meet in a public place
ask to meet in a public place

words.enDefinition: to be the first to show interest or do something about it

examples.en: I decided to make the first move and ask him about coffee after class.
examples.zh: 我决定「主动迈出第一步」，问他下课后要不要喝咖啡。

examples.en: They each hoped the other would make the first move at the club social.
examples.zh: 在社团聚会上，两人都希望对方「主动迈出第一步」。

collocations: decide to make the first move
wait for someone to make the first move
be willing to make the first move

words.enDefinition: to begin treating a romantic relationship as more committed

examples.en: They didn't plan to get serious until they knew where they'd be living in summer.
examples.zh: 在弄清楚暑假会住哪里之前，他们没打算「开始认真交往」。

examples.en: I asked what would change if we chose to get serious after the semester.
examples.zh: 我问如果学期结束后决定「开始认真交往」，会有哪些变化。

words.zhGloss: 有明确承诺的恋爱关系
words.enDefinition: an ongoing romantic relationship both people have agreed to value and maintain
acceptedZhAnswers: 有明确承诺的恋爱关系

examples.en: She wasn't sure she wanted a committed relationship during her year studying abroad.
examples.zh: 她不确定留学这一年里是否想进入「有明确承诺的恋爱关系」。

examples.en: They talked about what a committed relationship would mean while living in different cities.
examples.zh: 两人谈了异地居住时，「有明确承诺的恋爱关系」会意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: a romantic relationship that has lasted or is intended to last a long time

examples.en: He wanted a long-term relationship but hoped to take things slowly at the beginning.
examples.zh: 他想要一段「长期恋爱关系」，不过刚开始希望慢慢来。

examples.en: My roommate talked about maintaining a long-term relationship while finishing a degree abroad.
examples.zh: 室友聊起怎样在国外完成学位时维系「长期恋爱关系」。

words.enDefinition: a romantic relationship whose partners agree not to date other people

examples.en: They discussed an exclusive relationship before deciding how to introduce each other to friends.
examples.zh: 他们先讨论了是否建立「排他性恋爱关系」，再决定怎么向朋友介绍彼此。

examples.en: I wasn't ready for an exclusive relationship after only a few meetings in town.
examples.zh: 我们只在城里见了几次，我还没准备好进入「排他性恋爱关系」。

words.enDefinition: to have an ongoing romantic relationship with another person

examples.en: You don't have to be in a relationship to enjoy the campus film festival.
examples.zh: 不一定得「有恋爱对象」才能享受校园电影节。

examples.en: He didn't want to be in a relationship while adapting to the new course.
examples.zh: 他适应新课程时不想「谈恋爱」。

collocations: want to be in a relationship
choose to be in a relationship
be in a relationship with someone

words.enDefinition: the description of whether and how someone is romantically involved

examples.en: I left my relationship status off my profile because I preferred to keep it private.
examples.zh: 我希望这件事保密，所以没把「恋爱关系状态」放在个人资料里。

examples.en: They didn't discuss relationship status until both felt comfortable raising the subject in person.
examples.zh: 两人都觉得可以当面聊起这个话题时，才谈了「恋爱关系状态」。

words.enDefinition: to talk explicitly about what kind of romantic relationship two people have

examples.en: She wanted to define the relationship before committing to plans for the summer holidays.
examples.zh: 落实暑假计划前，她想「说清双方是什么关系」。

examples.en: They finally agreed to define the relationship after dating for most of the term.
examples.zh: 他们约会了大半个学期，最终同意「说清双方是什么关系」。

collocations: talk about whether to define the relationship

words.enDefinition: to explicitly agree that two people are a couple

examples.en: They decided to make it official after studying together for most of their exchange.
examples.zh: 一起学习了大半个交换期之后，他们决定「正式确定恋爱关系」。

examples.en: I wasn't ready to make it official just because our friends assumed we were dating.
examples.zh: 朋友以为我们在交往，可我还没准备好「正式确定恋爱关系」。

words.zhGloss: 没有明确关系的暧昧交往
words.enDefinition: an informal term for romantic involvement without a clearly defined relationship or commitment
acceptedZhAnswers: 没有明确关系的暧昧交往

examples.en: My friend described their situationship as somewhere between friendship and a committed relationship.
examples.zh: 朋友说，两人的「没有明确关系的暧昧交往」介于友情和正式恋爱之间。

examples.en: She wanted to understand where the situationship was going before making plans for next year.
examples.zh: 安排明年的计划前，她想弄清这段「没有明确关系的暧昧交往」接下来会怎样。

words.enDefinition: a person's established romantic partner, including a spouse

examples.en: The invitation said I could bring my significant other to the end-of-term dinner.
examples.zh: 邀请函上说，我可以带「亲密伴侣」参加学期末聚餐。

examples.en: Her significant other helped her pack the books before she moved for graduate school.
examples.zh: 她去外地读研前，「亲密伴侣」帮她把书装了起来。

words.enDefinition: an affectionate or humorous way to refer to one's romantic partner

examples.en: I asked my other half whether we still had time for coffee before the film.
examples.zh: 我问「我的另一半」，电影开场前我们还有没有时间喝咖啡。

examples.en: I told the group that my other half would join us once class ended.
examples.zh: 我告诉大家，「我的另一半」下课后会过来和我们会合。

words.enDefinition: two people who seem well suited to each other as partners

examples.en: Our friends thought we were a good match because we liked the same quiet places.
examples.zh: 朋友觉得我们是「合适的一对」，因为我们都喜欢同样的安静地方。

examples.en: They wondered whether they were a good match once their different plans became clear.
examples.zh: 各自的计划明朗后，两人想知道他们是否是「合适的一对」。

collocations: be a good match for each other

words.enDefinition: beliefs or principles that two people consider important in similar ways

examples.en: They talked about shared values before deciding where to live after university graduation.
examples.zh: 他们先谈了「共同的价值观」，再决定大学毕业后住在哪里。

examples.en: We agreed that shared values mattered more to us than liking the same films.
examples.zh: 我们一致觉得，「共同的价值观」比喜欢同样的电影更重要。

words.enDefinition: to set aside time to be together despite other duties

examples.en: We try to make time for each other even during the busiest weeks of term.
examples.zh: 即便在学期最忙的几周，我们也尽量「抽时间陪伴彼此」。

examples.en: They found ways to make time for each other while working opposite shifts.
examples.zh: 两人上班时间错开，还是想办法「抽时间陪伴彼此」。

collocations: try to make time for each other
find ways to make time for each other
remember to make time for each other

words.enDefinition: to be introduced to the parents of the person one is dating

examples.en: She felt ready to meet the parents during their short visit to the city.
examples.zh: 伴侣的父母来城里短住时，她觉得可以「去见对方的父母」了。

examples.en: I packed a spare shirt because I was going to meet the parents after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后要「见伴侣的父母」，就多带了一件衬衫。

collocations: be ready to meet the parents
first time you meet the parents

words.enDefinition: an important event marking a new stage in a romantic relationship

examples.en: Moving into the same city felt like a relationship milestone for both of them.
examples.zh: 搬到同一座城，对他们俩而言是个「恋爱关系的里程碑」。

examples.en: They celebrated a small relationship milestone with dinner at the place they first met.
examples.zh: 他们回第一次见面的地方吃饭，庆祝一个小小的「恋爱关系的里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: the yearly date when a couple marks the start of their dating relationship

examples.en: On our first dating anniversary, we went back to the cinema where we first met.
examples.zh: 第一次过「交往纪念日」时，我们回了最初见面的那家电影院。

examples.en: She remembered their dating anniversary after seeing an old photo from that weekend.
examples.zh: 看到那周末的一张旧照片后，她想起两人的「交往纪念日」。

words.enDefinition: to let other people know about a previously private romantic relationship

examples.en: They waited until graduation to go public with a relationship they had kept private all year.
examples.zh: 他们等到毕业才「公开了一整年都保密的恋爱关系」。

examples.en: I didn't want to go public with a relationship while we were still figuring things out.
examples.zh: 两人的想法还没理清时，我不想「公开恋爱关系」。

collocations: choose to go public with a relationship
decide when to go public with a relationship
ready to go public with a relationship

words.enDefinition: in informal social media usage, to hint at a romance without fully announcing it

examples.en: They decided to soft-launch a relationship by posting a photo of two coffees on campus.
examples.zh: 两人决定发一张校园里两杯咖啡的照片，「在网上低调透露恋情」。

examples.en: I didn't want to soft-launch a relationship before we'd even told our friends.
examples.zh: 我们还没告诉朋友，所以我不想「在网上低调透露恋情」。

collocations: soft-launch a relationship on social media

words.enDefinition: a limit someone sets to protect their comfort, privacy, or time

examples.en: Keeping their messages private was a personal boundary they discussed before dating seriously.
examples.zh: 不公开聊天记录，是他们认真交往前谈过的一条「个人界限」。

examples.en: My friend told me that Sunday study time was a personal boundary for her.
examples.zh: 朋友告诉我，周日的学习时间是她的一条「个人界限」。

words.enDefinition: to accept the limits another person states for their comfort or privacy

examples.en: Being able to respect someone's boundaries includes giving them the quiet time they ask for.
examples.zh: 对方明确说要独处时，给他们留出那段时间，也是在「尊重对方的界限」。

examples.en: It's important to respect someone's boundaries even when they differ from your own.
examples.zh: 即使对方的界限与你自己的不同，也要「尊重对方的界限」。

words.zhGloss: 问问伴侣的想法和情况
words.enDefinition: to contact your partner to see how they feel or how things are going
acceptedZhAnswers: 问问伴侣的想法和情况

examples.en: Try to check in with your partner before promising your whole weekend to friends.
examples.zh: 把整个周末都答应给朋友前，先「问问伴侣怎么想」。

examples.en: She said it's helpful to check in with your partner when your timetable changes.
examples.zh: 她说，课表变了时，「问问伴侣的想法和情况」会有帮助。

collocations: remember to check in with your partner
regularly check in with your partner
take time to check in with your partner

words.enDefinition: to discuss a situation in detail to understand it or decide what to do

examples.en: We went for a walk to talk things through before making a decision.
examples.zh: 我们出去走了走，先「把事情谈清楚」再做决定。

examples.en: He asked if there was time to talk things through after her evening class.
examples.zh: 他问她晚课后有没有时间「把事情谈清楚」。

collocations: take time to talk things through

words.enDefinition: to discuss a disagreement or misunderstanding so that tension eases

examples.en: I wanted to clear the air after my joke came across badly in the group chat.
examples.zh: 我在群里开的玩笑被误解后，想「消除彼此间的误会」。

examples.en: They met for coffee to clear the air before the campus festival that weekend.
examples.zh: 周末校园节庆之前，两人见面喝咖啡，好「消除彼此间的误会」。

words.enDefinition: to discuss conflicting views until you understand or resolve the problem

examples.en: They took a walk to work through a disagreement about their plans for summer.
examples.zh: 两人出去散步，想「通过沟通解决暑假计划上的分歧」。

examples.en: It was easier to work through a disagreement after they had both had lunch.
examples.zh: 都吃过午饭后，两人更容易「沟通解决分歧」了。

collocations: try to work through a disagreement
time to work through a disagreement
help to work through a disagreement

words.enDefinition: to allow someone time or privacy without pressing them to interact

examples.en: It's easier to give someone space when they tell you what they need.
examples.zh: 对方说清自己需要什么后，更容易「给对方一些独处空间」。

examples.en: She decided to give someone space after hearing that they needed some quiet time.
examples.zh: 听说对方需要安静一会儿后，她决定「给对方一些独处空间」。

words.enDefinition: to spend a period away from each other to consider a relationship

examples.en: They agreed to take some time apart before deciding whether to move in together.
examples.zh: 两人同意先「暂时各自冷静一段」，再决定是否一起住。

examples.en: We decided to take some time apart after struggling to balance travel and exams.
examples.zh: 因为在出行和考试之间难以兼顾，我们决定「暂时各自冷静一段」。

collocations: decide to take some time apart
agree to take some time apart
choose to take some time apart

words.enDefinition: temporarily apart by agreement while deciding about a romantic relationship

examples.en: They were on a break when our class went away for the field trip.
examples.zh: 我们班去实地考察时，他们的「恋爱关系暂时暂停」了。

examples.en: I didn't know we were on a break until we finally spoke about it.
examples.zh: 我们终于聊起这事时，我才知道我们的「恋爱关系暂时暂停」了。

collocations: spend time apart while on a break
agree to be on a break

words.enDefinition: a relationship that repeatedly ends and starts again

examples.en: They had an on-again, off-again relationship while studying for degrees in different cities.
examples.zh: 在不同城市读书时，他们有一段「分分合合的恋情」。

examples.en: My friend was tired of an on-again, off-again relationship by the end of summer.
examples.zh: 到暑假末，我朋友已经厌倦了那段「分分合合的恋情」。

collocations: be in an on-again, off-again relationship

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling romantic love for someone you previously loved

examples.en: I never thought we would fall out of love while living in the same city.
examples.zh: 我从没想到，我们住在同一座城市也会「渐渐不再爱了」。

examples.en: People sometimes fall out of love without either person doing anything particularly wrong.
examples.zh: 有时双方都没有做错什么，还是会「渐渐不再爱了」。

collocations: begin to fall out of love
fall out of love with someone

words.enDefinition: to decide to stop dating someone or end the relationship

examples.en: She chose to break things off before they applied to universities in different cities.
examples.zh: 在两人申请不同城市的学校之前，她选择「结束这段恋情」。

examples.en: He didn't know how to break things off without making their shared seminar awkward.
examples.zh: 他不知道怎样「结束这段恋情」，又不让两人一起上的研讨课变尴尬。

collocations: try to break things off gently

words.enDefinition: the end of a romantic relationship without hostility between the people involved

examples.en: They had an amicable breakup and stayed on friendly terms at their campus club.
examples.zh: 两人「和平分手」，在校园社团里仍能友好相处。

examples.en: An amicable breakup made it easier for them to share friends in the department.
examples.zh: 两人「和平分手」后，更容易继续和系里共同的朋友来往。

collocations: remain friendly after an amicable breakup

words.enDefinition: the end of a relationship agreed to by both partners

examples.en: They described it as a mutual breakup after months of talking about different priorities.
examples.zh: 讨论了几个月彼此不同的优先事项后，他们说这是「双方同意分手」。

examples.en: After the mutual breakup, both of them kept attending their usual weekly film club.
examples.zh: 「双方同意分手」之后，两人还是继续参加原来每周的电影社活动。

collocations: describe it as a mutual breakup

words.enDefinition: to continue to have a friendship after the nature of a relationship changes

examples.en: They hoped to remain friends after they both decided the relationship was over.
examples.zh: 两人都决定结束恋情后，希望「仍然做朋友」。

examples.en: It was important for them to remain friends because they shared so many classes.
examples.zh: 两人有很多共同的课，所以「仍然做朋友」对他们很重要。

words.enDefinition: to maintain a friendly or civil relationship after a change or disagreement

examples.en: They managed to stay on good terms after they stopped seeing each other.
examples.zh: 两人不再交往后，还是能「保持客气友好的关系」。

examples.en: I hoped we could stay on good terms and greet each other in the lab.
examples.zh: 我希望我们能「保持客气友好的关系」，在实验室见面可以打个招呼。

collocations: manage to stay on good terms
want to stay on good terms
stay on good terms with someone

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling upset about a person after a relationship or interest ends

examples.en: It took a while to get over someone I still saw in class every week.
examples.zh: 我每周上课还会见到对方，花了好一阵才「走出那段感情」。

examples.en: My friend said it was harder to get over someone when all their friends overlapped.
examples.zh: 朋友说，两人的朋友都是同一拨人时，更难「走出对某人的感情」。

collocations: take time to get over someone

words.enDefinition: a person with whom someone formerly had a romantic relationship

examples.en: My ex-partner and I still say hello when we meet outside the library.
examples.zh: 我和「前任伴侣」在图书馆外遇到时还是会打招呼。

examples.en: She asked her ex-partner to return the books they had bought for their course.
examples.zh: 她请「前任伴侣」还回两人为课程买的那些书。

words.enDefinition: still affected by a recent breakup, especially when starting to date again

examples.en: She wondered whether she was on the rebound when she started dating again that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天重新约会时，她怀疑自己是不是「仍受刚分手的影响」。

examples.en: He didn't want to go on another date while he was still on the rebound.
examples.zh: 他不想在「仍受刚分手的影响」时接着去约会。

collocations: meet someone while on the rebound

words.zhGloss: 分手后迅速开始的恋情
words.enDefinition: a relationship started soon after a breakup, often before the earlier feelings fade
acceptedZhAnswers: 分手后迅速开始的恋情

examples.en: Her friend asked whether it felt like a rebound relationship after such a short break.
examples.zh: 间隔这么短，朋友问她是否觉得那是段「分手后迅速开始的恋情」。

examples.en: They talked about whether a rebound relationship could turn into something more serious over time.
examples.zh: 他们谈到，「分手后迅速开始的恋情」能否随着时间发展成更认真的关系。

words.enDefinition: to revive a romantic connection that has weakened or ended

examples.en: They hoped to rekindle a relationship after moving back to the same city for work.
examples.zh: 两人工作后搬回同一座城，希望能「重新培养感情」。

examples.en: She wasn't sure whether to rekindle a relationship with someone she had dated before university.
examples.zh: 她不确定是否要和大学前交往过的人「重新培养感情」。

words.enDefinition: to become a couple again after a romantic breakup

examples.en: They decided to get back together after spending the summer in different places.
examples.zh: 在不同地方过完暑假后，两人决定「复合」。

examples.en: I didn't expect them to get back together when they returned for their final year.
examples.zh: 我没想到他们回来读最后一学年时会「复合」。

words.enDefinition: to make another attempt at a relationship after difficulties or a breakup

examples.en: They decided to give things another try after discussing what had gone wrong last term.
examples.zh: 他们谈过上学期出了什么问题后，决定「再试着交往一次」。

examples.en: She wondered whether to give things another try when he reached out over the summer.
examples.zh: 暑假他主动联系她时，她犹豫要不要「再试着交往一次」。

collocations: agree to give things another try
decide to give things another try
ready to give things another try

words.enDefinition: suddenly stopping all communication with someone without explaining why

examples.en: My friend thought it was ghosting when the conversation stopped immediately after their date.
examples.zh: 两人约完后对话突然中断，朋友觉得对方是「突然断联」了。

examples.en: They talked about ghosting when someone in the group mentioned a date that went quiet.
examples.zh: 小组里有人提到约会对象忽然没了消息，大家便聊起「突然断联」。

words.enDefinition: a period or arrangement in which people do not communicate with each other

examples.en: They agreed to no contact for a while after their relationship ended in spring.
examples.zh: 春天结束恋情后，两人约好一段时间「完全停止联系」。

examples.en: She wanted no contact during exams so she could focus on finishing the term.
examples.zh: 她想在考试期间「完全停止联系」，好专心完成这学期的学业。

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling attracted to someone or wanting to continue seeing them

examples.en: He began to lose interest when their conversations became less frequent over the summer.
examples.zh: 暑假里两人聊得越来越少，他开始「不再感兴趣」。

examples.en: They wondered why people sometimes lose interest after a few dates despite getting along well.
examples.zh: 他们想知道，为什么有时几次约会相处得不错，人还是会「不再感兴趣」。

words.expression: I can't see this going anywhere
words.lemma: i can't see this going anywhere
words.zhGloss: 我看不到这段关系的未来
words.enDefinition: a phrase saying you do not expect the relationship to develop further
acceptedZhAnswers: 我看不到这段关系的未来
acceptedEnVariants: I can't see this going anywhere
I cannot see this going anywhere

examples.en: “I can't see this going anywhere,” he wrote after their conversation about next year.
examples.zh: 谈过明年的计划后，他写道：“「我看不到这段关系的未来」。”

examples.en: I finally said, “I can't see this going anywhere,” during our walk back to campus.
examples.zh: 走回学校的路上，我终于说：“「我看不到这段关系的未来」。”

collocations: honestly, I can't see this going anywhere
I can't see this going anywhere right now
I can't see this going anywhere long term

words.expression: I only see you as a friend
words.lemma: i only see you as a friend
words.enDefinition: a kind but direct way to say you do not feel romantic interest
acceptedEnVariants: I only see you as a friend

examples.en: “I only see you as a friend,” she said when he asked about another date.
examples.zh: 他问要不要再约一次，她说：“「我只把你当朋友」。”

examples.en: I told him, “I only see you as a friend, and I didn't want to pretend.”
examples.zh: 我告诉他：“「我只把你当朋友」，我不想假装有别的感情。”

collocations: I only see you as a friend right now
honestly, I only see you as a friend
I think I only see you as a friend

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying two people have different hopes for their lives or relationship

examples.en: “We want different things,” she said after they compared their plans for next year.
examples.zh: 比过明年的计划后，她说：“「我们想要的不一样」。”

examples.en: I told a friend that we want different things and had decided to stop dating.
examples.zh: 我告诉朋友，「我们想要的不一样」，已经决定不再交往。

collocations: we want different things in life
we want different things right now
I think we want different things

words.enDefinition: a statement that someone feels content without a romantic relationship

examples.en: “I'm happy being single,” my flatmate said when we asked about the dating event.
examples.zh: 我们问起单身交友活动时，室友说：“「我享受单身生活」。”

examples.en: I told her, “I'm happy being single while I get used to living here.”
examples.zh: 我告诉她：“我还在适应这里的生活，「我享受单身生活」。”

collocations: I'm happy being single right now
I'm happy being single while I finish my degree

words.enDefinition: not in a relationship because you prefer to remain single

examples.en: She described herself as single by choice while finishing the final year of her degree.
examples.zh: 她在读学位最后一年时，说自己是「主动选择单身」。

examples.en: My roommate was single by choice and enjoyed meeting people as friends through clubs.
examples.zh: 室友「主动选择单身」，喜欢通过社团结交朋友。

collocations: describe yourself as single by choice

words.enDefinition: the people, places, and social habits involved in dating in a particular setting

examples.en: My friend was curious about the dating scene after moving to a smaller university town.
examples.zh: 朋友搬到较小的大学城后，很好奇当地的「交友约会圈」怎么样。

examples.en: We talked about the dating scene while walking back from the student film night.
examples.zh: 我们从学生电影之夜走回来时聊了「当地交友约会圈」。

collocations: get back into the dating scene

words.enDefinition: information about the romantic relationships someone has previously had

examples.en: They didn't discuss relationship history until they knew each other well enough to feel comfortable.
examples.zh: 两人熟到觉得自在后才聊「过往恋爱经历」。

examples.en: I chose to leave my relationship history out of the conversation that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，我选择不在谈话中提到「过往恋爱经历」。

collocations: share part of your relationship history

words.enDefinition: something done to show affection or romantic interest to another person

examples.en: Bringing tea to the library felt like a romantic gesture during the exam period.
examples.zh: 考试期间送茶来图书馆，感觉是个「表达爱意的举动」。

examples.en: He kept the silly postcard because he had understood it as a romantic gesture.
examples.zh: 他留着那张搞怪的明信片，因为觉得那是「表达爱意的举动」。

words.enDefinition: to make your fondness or care for someone visible through words or actions

examples.en: They had different ways to show affection when they were around their classmates.
examples.zh: 在同学面前，两人「表达亲近和喜爱」的方式不同。

examples.en: I learned that he liked to show affection by remembering small details I mentioned.
examples.zh: 我知道了，他喜欢记住我提到的小事来「表达亲近和喜爱」。

words.enDefinition: time spent together with attention that helps strengthen a relationship

examples.en: We set aside some quality time after exams and cooked lunch together at home.
examples.zh: 考试后，我们专门留了点「专心相处的时光」，一起在家做午饭。

examples.en: She suggested turning off their phones so they could have some quality time together.
examples.zh: 她建议关掉手机，好有一点「专心相处的时光」。

words.enDefinition: to move forward to a more committed stage of a relationship

examples.en: They wanted to take the next step after finding work in the same city.
examples.zh: 在同一座城找到工作后，两人想「让关系更进一步」。

examples.en: I asked what it would mean to take the next step in our relationship.
examples.zh: 我问在我们的恋爱里，「让关系更进一步」意味着什么。

collocations: be ready to take the next step
decide to take the next step
want to take the next step

words.enDefinition: to begin sharing private feelings or worries with the person you are dating

examples.en: It can take time to open up to your partner about worries from home.
examples.zh: 要「向伴侣说出有关家里的心里话」，有时需要一点时间。

examples.en: My friend said it helped to open up to your partner when work became stressful.
examples.zh: 朋友说，工作压力变大时，「向伴侣说出心里话」会有帮助。

collocations: find time to open up to your partner
learn to open up to your partner
feel safe to open up to your partner

words.enDefinition: to decide not to share personal matters with a wider group of people

examples.en: We chose to keep things private until both of us felt ready to tell friends.
examples.zh: 在两人都准备好告诉朋友之前，我们选择「不公开关系细节」。

examples.en: They agreed to keep things private even after their classmates knew they were dating.
examples.zh: 即使同学知道他们在交往，两人仍同意「不公开关系细节」。

words.expression: can we talk about where this is going
words.lemma: can we talk about where this is going
words.zhGloss: 我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗
words.enDefinition: a question asking to discuss how the relationship might develop in the future
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗
acceptedEnVariants: can we talk about where this is going

examples.en: At the café I asked, “Can we talk about where this is going before next term?”
examples.zh: 我在咖啡馆问：“下学期开学前，「我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗」？”

examples.en: “Can we talk about where this is going?” he asked on the walk back from class.
examples.zh: 下课往回走时，他问：“「我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗」？”

collocations: can we talk about where this is going tonight
can we talk about where this is going sometime
can we talk about where this is going next term

words.enDefinition: to accept another person's choice even when you had hoped for a different outcome

examples.en: “I respect your decision,” he said when she told him she wasn't ready to date.
examples.zh: 她说还没做好约会的准备，他答道：“我「尊重你的决定」。”

examples.en: I replied, “I respect your decision to wait until after the exams to talk.”
examples.zh: 我回答：“你决定等考试后再谈，我「尊重你的决定」。”

collocations: I respect your decision about this

words.enDefinition: an action showing romantic affection that other people in public can see

examples.en: They talked about what counted as a public display of affection near the residence.
examples.zh: 两人聊到，在宿舍附近哪些行为算「公开场合的亲密举动」。

examples.en: A quick hug was the only public display of affection that either felt comfortable with.
examples.zh: 两人都只接受短暂拥抱这类「公开场合的亲密举动」。

collocations: a brief public display of affection
comfortable with a public display of affection
avoid a public display of affection

words.enDefinition: to be introduced to the people close to one's romantic partner

examples.en: We decided to meet each other's friends at the café after our last exam.
examples.zh: 我们决定最后一门考试后在咖啡馆「见见彼此的朋友」。

examples.en: They thought it would be easier to meet each other's friends at a casual picnic.
examples.zh: 他们觉得轻松的野餐更适合「见见彼此的朋友」。

collocations: be ready to meet each other's friends
plan to meet each other's friends
first time you meet each other's friends

words.enDefinition: a close, affectionate relationship without a sexual element, often a friendship

examples.en: She explained that theirs was a platonic relationship when a classmate assumed they were dating.
examples.zh: 同学以为他们在交往，她解释说，两人是「纯友谊关系」。

examples.en: They had a close platonic relationship and often went to films together after lectures.
examples.zh: 他们是关系很好的「纯友谊关系」，下课后常一起看电影。

collocations: describe it as a platonic relationship

words.enDefinition: plans or hopes for the life two people might have together

examples.en: They imagined a shared future after finding work in the same part of town.
examples.zh: 在城里同一区域找到工作后，两人想象起了「共同的未来」。

examples.en: We talked about a shared future while walking home from the graduation reception.
examples.zh: 毕业招待会后走回家的路上，我们聊到「共同的未来」。

words.enDefinition: to share your feelings openly with the person they concern

examples.en: It takes courage to tell someone how you feel before you know their response.
examples.zh: 不知道对方会怎么答时，「把感受告诉对方」需要勇气。

examples.en: My friend said it's easier to tell someone how you feel somewhere quiet and familiar.
examples.zh: 朋友说，在安静熟悉的地方更容易「把感受告诉对方」。

collocations: want to tell someone how you feel
decide to tell someone how you feel
find time to tell someone how you feel

words.enDefinition: to explain openly what you expect so that the other person understands

examples.en: They decided to set clear expectations about how often they would see each other.
examples.zh: 两人决定「说清各自的期待」，说明希望多久见一次。

examples.en: It helped to set clear expectations before they planned a holiday together in June.
examples.zh: 六月一起安排假期前，「说清各自的期待」让事情更顺利。

collocations: set clear expectations about a relationship

words.enDefinition: to show such intense interest that it may make another person uncomfortable

examples.en: He worried he might come on too strong by suggesting another date before leaving.
examples.zh: 他担心离开前就提下次约会，会「一上来表现得太热切」。

examples.en: I didn't want to come on too strong when we had only talked once.
examples.zh: 我们只聊过一次，我不想「一上来表现得太热切」。

collocations: try not to come on too strong
worry about coming on too strong
seem to come on too strong
